trust_decision.summary: The panel must confine the file destinations Xray writes to (log.access / log.error, taken verbatim from the stored xrayTemplateConfig) inside config.GetLogFolder(); the decision is made when the runtime config is generated, in resolveXrayLogPaths, not when the template is saved.

landing_point.why: The summary's 'Xray Log Path Manipulation' is only reachable by posting a full template to the settings save route (POST /panel/api/xray/update, registered at internal/web/controller/xray_setting.go:48 and internal/web/controller/api.go:88), so an engineer starts at that handler and follows it to the log block of the template.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /panel/api/xray/update (XraySettingController.updateSetting) and POST /panel/api/server/importDB (ServerController.importDB), both reaching XrayService.RestartXray -> GetXrayConfig; also POST /panel/api/server/restartXrayService re-runs the same generation on an already-stored template

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The code documents the escaping shapes as intentional: absolute values are skipped outright (internal/web/service/xray.go:524-526) and the comment at internal/web/service/xray.go:532-534 says a nested relative path like ./logs/foo.log is 'a deliberate user choice and left alone', so a solver can treat an admin-chosen /etc/... or ../ path as supported configuration rather than the bug; the same reading lets a solver exclude the DB-import entry point on the grounds that the panel's own backup/restore is trusted admin input.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Values that mean 'no file' must stay exactly as written: the shipped default template carries access "none" and error "" (internal/web/service/config.json:20-25) and those two spellings are skipped at internal/web/service/xray.go:521-523; an over-broad confinement rewrites them to /var/log/x-ui/none and starts logging every proxied connection on default deployments. A second legitimate value is an admin-chosen absolute path (honoured at internal/web/service/xray.go:524-526), which the panel itself reads back to find the access log (internal/xray/process.go:79-99 used by internal/web/service/server.go:999-1007 and the IP-limit job), so dropping or redirecting the whole log block silently changes where access-log parsing and IP limiting look.

O6_input_shapes: absolute POSIX path (/etc/cron.d/x) - previously left untouched, now reduced to its base and confined
nested relative path (logs/foo.log) - previously left untouched as a 'deliberate user choice', now flattened to its base
non-string JSON value for access/error - left untouched (only strings are rewritten)
unparseable or absent log block - left untouched

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second hand-built xray.Config whose log block is taken from the panel template instead of being hardcoded, started through xray.NewTestProcess (internal/web/service/outbound/outbound.go:370-385).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This builder already sets a log block by hand (access "none", error "") and starts a real xray process from a user-supplied outbound, so a maintainer adding 'show the probe's log' would copy the template value here; it sits in a different package from resolveXrayLogPaths, so the confinement never runs.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A path confinement added to CheckXrayConfig (save-time validation) rather than to the generation helper.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: CheckXrayConfig is the function named for validating the template and is the obvious place to 'also validate the log paths'; it is bypassed by the DB-import route, which replaces the settings row without ever calling it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another read of the raw template that extracts one field (discoverListen reads metrics.listen) and acts on it directly.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file shows the codebase will parse the stored template directly when it needs a single value; a sibling that reads log.access the same way (e.g. a log-tail preview) would bypass GetXrayConfig entirely.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A caller of the low-level NewProcess with an xray.Config carrying an unconfined log block.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Process is the public constructor for the sink and performs no log-path checks at all (internal/xray/process.go:486-517 writes the config and runs the core), so the protection lives entirely one layer above it.

O9_family: externally controlled file path leading to arbitrary file write (CWE-73 / CWE-20), configuration-tampering variant

O10_build.toolchain: Go 1.26.4 with cgo/gcc (mattn/go-sqlite3); Node/npm because internal/web embeds all:dist (internal/web/web.go:47) and no internal/web/dist tree is committed, so the frontend must be built before go build ./...
O10_build.project_tests: internal/web/service/xray_config_inject_test.go (config-generation unit tests over a temporary DB), internal/web/service/xray_setting_test.go (SaveXraySetting/UnwrapXrayTemplateConfig), internal/xray/config_test.go and internal/xray/hot_diff_test.go, internal/web/job/check_client_ip_job_test.go (fake xray binary via a script); no test at the pinned commit covers resolveXrayLogPaths

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the confinement to SaveXraySetting/CheckXrayConfig (the settings-page save path) instead of the generation helper in GetXrayConfig, which leaves the DB-import entry point open, or simply reject absolute paths while keeping the 'nested relative is a deliberate choice' branch.
